guideWhatIsAvif.title: What Is AVIF? Browser Support & How to Convert
guideWhatIsAvif.description: A comprehensive guide to the AVIF image format, browser compatibility, and conversion methods.
guideWhatIsAvif.intro: AVIF (AV1 Image File Format) is a next-generation image format based on the AV1 video codec, developed by the Alliance for Open Media (AOMedia). It offers significantly better compression than JPEG and WebP while maintaining excellent image quality. In this guide, we will explain what AVIF is, which browsers support it, and how to convert your images to AVIF.
guideWhatIsAvif.whatIsAvifText: AVIF is an open, royalty-free image format that uses the AV1 video codec for image compression. It was first released in 2019 and has rapidly gained adoption due to its superior compression efficiency.
guideWhatIsAvif.whatIsAvifFeature1Text: AVIF files are typically 50% smaller than JPEG and 20% smaller than WebP at the same visual quality. This translates to faster page loads and lower bandwidth costs.
guideWhatIsAvif.whatIsAvifFeature2Text: AVIF supports HDR and wide color gamuts (up to 12-bit color depth), making it ideal for photography and media-rich websites.
guideWhatIsAvif.whatIsAvifFeature3Text: Like PNG and WebP, AVIF supports alpha transparency. It also supports animated images, serving as a modern alternative to GIF.
guideWhatIsAvif.browserSupportText: As of early 2026, AVIF is supported by all major browsers:
guideWhatIsAvif.browserNote: AVIF now has over 95% global browser coverage, making it safe to use for most web projects. For the remaining browsers, you can provide JPEG or WebP fallbacks using the HTML picture element.
guideWhatIsAvif.conversionMethodsTitle: 3 Ways to Convert Images to AVIF
guideWhatIsAvif.method1Text: The easiest way to convert images to AVIF is using an online converter like QuickConv. Simply upload your image, select AVIF as the output format, and download the result. No software installation required.
guideWhatIsAvif.method1Steps: Upload your JPG, PNG, or WebP file. Select AVIF as the target format. Click "Start Conversion" and download the result.
guideWhatIsAvif.method2Text: For batch processing or automation, you can use command-line tools. FFmpeg supports AVIF encoding with the libaom-av1 codec. The libavif library also provides the avifenc tool for direct AVIF encoding.
guideWhatIsAvif.method3Text: Adobe Photoshop (2024+) and GIMP (2.10.32+) support AVIF export natively. In Photoshop, use File > Export > Save for Web and select AVIF. In GIMP, use File > Export As and choose AVIF from the format list.
guideWhatIsAvif.conclusionText: AVIF is the most efficient image format available today, offering the best balance of quality and file size. With over 95% browser support, there is no reason not to start using it. If you want to quickly convert your images to AVIF, try QuickConv for free.

guideHeicToJpg.title: 3 Ways to Convert iPhone HEIC Photos to JPG
guideHeicToJpg.description: A practical guide to converting HEIC photos from your iPhone to the universally compatible JPG format.
guideHeicToJpg.intro: If you own an iPhone, you have probably encountered HEIC files when transferring photos to a Windows PC or sharing them online. HEIC is Apple's default photo format since iOS 11, and while it offers great compression, it is not universally compatible. This guide explains what HEIC is, why Apple uses it, and three easy ways to convert HEIC to JPG.
guideHeicToJpg.whatIsHeicText: HEIC (High Efficiency Image Container) is a file format based on the HEIF (High Efficiency Image Format) standard, which uses the HEVC (H.265) video codec for still image compression. Apple adopted HEIC as the default photo format for iPhone starting with iOS 11 in 2017.
guideHeicToJpg.whyIphoneText: Apple chose HEIC for several compelling reasons:
guideHeicToJpg.whyIphoneReason1: File Size: HEIC files are roughly 50% smaller than equivalent JPG files, saving significant storage space on your device.
guideHeicToJpg.whyIphoneReason2: Quality: Despite the smaller file size, HEIC maintains better image quality than JPG, with support for 16-bit color depth.
guideHeicToJpg.whyIphoneReason3: Features: HEIC supports transparency, image sequences (Live Photos), and depth maps that JPG cannot store.
guideHeicToJpg.problemText: While HEIC is excellent, many platforms and applications still do not support it natively. Windows 10/11 requires a paid codec extension, most web platforms do not accept HEIC uploads, and many photo editing tools cannot open HEIC files. Converting to JPG solves all of these compatibility issues.
guideHeicToJpg.method1Text: The fastest and most convenient way to convert HEIC to JPG is using an online converter. QuickConv lets you convert HEIC photos directly in your browser with no software installation.
guideHeicToJpg.method1Step1: Visit QuickConv and select the HEIC to JPG converter.
guideHeicToJpg.method1Step2: Drag and drop your HEIC file or click to select it from your device.
guideHeicToJpg.method1Step3: Click "Start Conversion" to begin the process.
guideHeicToJpg.method1Advantage: QuickConv automatically deletes your files after 24 hours for privacy. No account registration or watermark.
guideHeicToJpg.method2Text: If you are on a Mac, you can use the built-in Preview app to convert HEIC to JPG:
guideHeicToJpg.method2Step1: Open the HEIC file in Preview (double-click the file).
guideHeicToJpg.method2Step2: Go to File > Export from the menu bar.
guideHeicToJpg.method2Step3: Select JPEG as the format and adjust the quality slider.
guideHeicToJpg.method2Step4: Choose a save location and click Save.
guideHeicToJpg.method2Note: This method works well for individual files but can be tedious for batch conversion of many photos.
guideHeicToJpg.method3Text: You can configure your iPhone to always use JPG instead of HEIC for future photos:
guideHeicToJpg.method3Note: Note: This will increase the file size of your photos by approximately 2x. This setting only affects new photos; existing HEIC photos are not converted.
guideHeicToJpg.conclusionText: HEIC is a great format for storage efficiency, but JPG remains the most universally compatible image format. For quick, hassle-free conversion, we recommend using QuickConv's online HEIC to JPG converter. It is free, private, and works on any device with a browser.

guideWebpVsAvifVsHeic.title: WebP vs AVIF vs HEIC: Next-Gen Image Format Comparison
guideWebpVsAvifVsHeic.description: A detailed comparison of the three major next-generation image formats to help you choose the right one.
guideWebpVsAvifVsHeic.intro: The traditional JPEG and PNG formats have dominated the web for decades, but next-generation formats like WebP, AVIF, and HEIC offer dramatically better compression and features. Each has its strengths and ideal use cases. This guide provides a comprehensive comparison to help you decide which format to use and when.
guideWebpVsAvifVsHeic.webpText: Developed by Google in 2010, WebP is based on the VP8/VP9 video codec. It was the first widely-adopted next-gen image format and is now supported by all major browsers. WebP offers 25-34% smaller files than JPEG with lossy compression and 26% smaller files than PNG with lossless compression.
guideWebpVsAvifVsHeic.avifText: Released in 2019 by the Alliance for Open Media, AVIF is based on the AV1 video codec. It offers the best compression ratio among the three formats, typically 50% smaller than JPEG. AVIF supports HDR, wide color gamut, and film grain synthesis, making it the most feature-rich option.
guideWebpVsAvifVsHeic.heicText: HEIC (High Efficiency Image Container) uses the HEVC (H.265) codec for compression. It is Apple's default photo format on iOS and macOS since 2017. HEIC offers similar compression to WebP but has limited browser support due to HEVC patent licensing requirements.
guideWebpVsAvifVsHeic.browserSupportText: Browser support is a critical factor for web use:
guideWebpVsAvifVsHeic.browserWebpSupport: WebP: 97%+ global support. All modern browsers since 2020.
guideWebpVsAvifVsHeic.browserAvifSupport: AVIF: 95%+ global support. Chrome 85+, Firefox 93+, Safari 16.4+, Edge 121+.
guideWebpVsAvifVsHeic.browserHeicSupport: HEIC: Very limited. Only Safari on macOS/iOS natively. Chrome and Firefox do not support HEIC. Not recommended for web use.
guideWebpVsAvifVsHeic.compressionText: When compressing a typical photograph to similar visual quality (SSIM), the formats compare as follows:
guideWebpVsAvifVsHeic.compressionNote: AVIF consistently produces the smallest files, followed by HEIC, then WebP. However, AVIF encoding is slower than WebP encoding, which can be a consideration for real-time conversion.
guideWebpVsAvifVsHeic.useCaseWebText: Best choice: AVIF with WebP fallback. Use the picture element to serve AVIF to supporting browsers and WebP to the rest. This gives you the best compression with universal compatibility.
guideWebpVsAvifVsHeic.useCasePhotoText: Best choice: AVIF (lossless). AVIF's 12-bit color depth and HDR support make it ideal for preserving photo quality. For Apple ecosystem users, HEIC is also a good option.
guideWebpVsAvifVsHeic.useCaseMobileText: Best choice: HEIC (default on iPhone). If you need to share with non-Apple users, convert to JPG or WebP using a tool like QuickConv.
guideWebpVsAvifVsHeic.useCaseSocialText: Best choice: JPG or WebP. Most social media platforms re-encode uploaded images anyway, so compatibility matters more than compression. Use WebP for the best balance.
guideWebpVsAvifVsHeic.conversionText: QuickConv supports conversion between all three next-generation formats and traditional formats like JPG and PNG. You can convert WebP to AVIF, HEIC to JPG, AVIF to PNG, and many more combinations with just a few clicks.
guideWebpVsAvifVsHeic.conclusionText: Each format has its place: WebP for maximum compatibility, AVIF for maximum compression and quality, and HEIC for the Apple ecosystem. For web use, AVIF with a WebP fallback is the recommended strategy in 2026. Use QuickConv to easily convert between all these formats for free.
